problem: Fresh local food from small producers was hard to buy; Membo delivered next day from producers directly.

exit.reason: Registry aggregator shows bankruptcy with a trustee appointed Sep 19, 2023; no company statement

competitors.name: Wolt (with Rimi)
competitors.what: Grocery delivery from Rimi stores in Tallinn

competitors.name: Bolt Market
competitors.what: Grocery delivery via Bolt Food app

technical_complexity.rationale: Consumer app plus logistics orchestration; mostly operational.

defensibility.rationale: Low barriers: producer relationships and delivery could be copied by quick commerce players.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Bolt Market and Wolt/Rimi launched grocery delivery in Tallinn in Aug and Sep 2021.

market_need_then: YC page says 30% monthly growth over eight months and over 4,000 orders in Tallinn.

brand_strength.rationale: Short, distinctive name; no brand press found.

outcome_analysis: Membo grew orders in Tallinn quickly after launching in December 2020 and joined YC in Summer 2021, but quick commerce giants Bolt and Wolt entered grocery delivery the same year. Registry data points to bankruptcy in 2023. No founder statement exists, so the failure factors reflect competition and thin margins as likely causes only.
notes: Pre-seed amount rests on Seedtable and CB Insights (two databases, $130K, which equals the standard YC deal); the TechCrunch article snippet did not state an amount. Bankruptcy rests on a registry aggregator only. Competitor sources Aug and Sept 2021 are within the batch period, a few months after as_of. Failure factors are inferred. membo.ee fetch returned only a title.
